lines.text: How big is Earth's water? Gather every drop into one ball, and measure it.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ bˈɪɡ ɪz ˈɜːθz wˈɔːɾɚ? ɡˈæðɚɹ ˈɛvɹi dɹˈɑːp ˌɪntʊ wˈʌn bˈɔːl, ænd mˈɛʒɚɹ ɪt.

lines.text: Count the oceans, the ice, the lakes, the rivers, the water underground, and the water in the air. It adds up to about one point four billion cubic kilometers.
lines.phonemes: kˈaʊnt ðɪ ˈoʊʃənz, ðɪ ˈaɪs, ðə lˈeɪks, ðə ɹˈɪvɚz, ðə wˈɔːɾɚɹ ˌʌndɚɡɹˈaʊnd, ænd ðə wˈɔːɾɚɹ ɪnðɪ ˈɛɹ. ɪɾ ˈædz ˌʌp tʊ ɐbˌaʊt wˈʌn pˈɔɪnt fˈɔːɹ bˈɪliən kjˈuːbɪk kɪlˈɑːmɪɾɚz.

lines.text: Squeeze all of it into one round ball, as if it were a single giant drop. That ball is about fourteen hundred kilometers wide.
lines.phonemes: skwˈiːz ˈɔːl ʌv ɪɾ ˌɪntʊ wˈʌn ɹˈaʊnd bˈɔːl, æz ɪf ɪt wɜːɹ ɐ sˈɪŋɡəl dʒˈaɪənt dɹˈɑːp. ðæt bˈɔːl ɪz ɐbˌaʊt fˈɔːɹtiːn hˈʌndɹɪd kɪlˈɑːmɪɾɚz wˈaɪd.

lines.text: That sounds enormous, and next to us it is. But our world is much bigger, so let's set the ball next to a planet.
lines.phonemes: ðæt sˈaʊndz ɪnˈɔːɹməs, ænd nˈɛkst tʊ ˌʌs ɪɾ ˈɪz. bˌʌt ˌaʊɚ wˈɜːld ɪz mˈʌtʃ bˈɪɡɚ, sˌoʊ lˈɛts sˈɛt ðə bˈɔːl nˈɛkst tʊ ɐ plˈænɪt.

lines.text: It is less than half as wide as the Moon. Next to the Earth, it is a marble beside a basketball.
lines.phonemes: ɪɾ ɪz lˈɛs ðɐn hˈæf æz wˈaɪd æz ðə mˈuːn. nˈɛkst tə ðɪ ˈɜːθ, ɪɾ ɪz ɐ mˈɑːɹbəl bᵻsˌaɪd ɐ bˈæskɪtbˌɔːl.

lines.text: Only a small part of the water is fresh; count just that, and the ball is about four hundred kilometers wide.
lines.phonemes: ˈoʊnli ɐ smˈɔːl pˈɑːɹt ʌvðə wˈɔːɾɚɹ ɪz fɹˈɛʃ; kˈaʊnt dʒˈʌst ðˈæt, ænd ðə bˈɔːl ɪz ɐbˌaʊt fˈɔːɹ hˈʌndɹɪd kɪlˈɑːmɪɾɚz wˈaɪd.

lines.text: Earth looks like a water world from space. But its water is only about an eighth of one percent of its volume.
lines.phonemes: ˈɜːθ lˈʊks lˈaɪk ɐ wˈɔːɾɚ wˈɜːld fɹʌm spˈeɪs. bˌʌt ɪts wˈɔːɾɚɹ ɪz ˈoʊnli ɐbˌaʊt ɐn ˈeɪtθ ʌv wˈʌn pɚsˈɛnt ʌv ɪts vˈɑːljuːm.

lines.text: Next envelope: could we catch all the world's lightning?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst ˈɑːnvəlˌoʊp: kʊd wiː kˈætʃ ˈɔːl ðə wˈɜːldz lˈaɪtnɪŋ?
